answer: The sample is committed in advance and revealed afterwards, and identities that signed the sampled transaction cannot verify it, so verification is always performed by a party with no stake in the outcome. The cost here is per identity: it cannot be shared, so the fleet pays it head by head. One voyage is drawn blind, one mirror must sign it without stake, and the tundra proves the draw was fair: the farm can file a thousand claims but only the voyage subset is ever checked, and each of those needs a mirror it does not own. The verifier must also be independent of the transactor.
